title: Bench Grinder Safety
summary: A bench grinder is safe only when its guards, work rest and wheel are set up right. This talk follows OSHA's grinder checklist. The side-guard and tongue-guard figures come from the general-industry standard 29 CFR 1910.215; the construction rule is 29 CFR 1926.303.
talking_points: Side guards must cover the spindle, nut and flange and 75% of the wheel diameter.
Keep the work rest adjusted to within 1/8-inch of the wheel. Adjust it only when the wheel is stopped.
Keep the adjustable tongue guard on the top of the grinder within 1/4-inch of the wheel.
The maximum RPM rating of each wheel must be compatible with the RPM rating of the grinder motor.
Before mounting a new wheel, inspect it and ring test it.
Always wear goggles or a face shield when grinding.
Bench and pedestal grinders must be permanently mounted, and each grinder needs an individual on and off switch and a continuous path to ground.
Keep the area around the grinder clean, and use dust collectors or powered exhaust where grinding makes a lot of dust.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing or damaged side guard or tongue guard
Work rest set wider than 1/8-inch from the wheel
Tongue guard set wider than 1/4-inch from the wheel
Grinder not permanently mounted, or without an on and off switch
Wheel with cracks, or rated for a lower RPM than the motor
Grinding dust or clutter building up around the machine
discussion_questions: How close is the work rest on our grinder, and who checks it?
What is the ring test, and when do we do it?
What eye protection is required every time we grind?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA's Machine Guarding Checklist for Abrasive Wheel Equipment Grinders (from OSHA Publication 2209). Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: All points quote-accurate to the OSHA Abrasive Wheel Grinder checklist (75% side guard, 1/8-inch work rest, 1/4-inch tongue guard, RPM match, ring test, goggles/face shield, permanent mount, individual switch, ground, housekeeping, dust collection).

FIX MADE: the 75% side-guard and 1/4-inch tongue-guard specifics come from general-industry 29 CFR 1910.215 (source cites it). 29 CFR 1926.303 (verified) is the construction equivalent for grinder guarding, ring test, and the 1/8-inch work rest, but does not restate the tongue guard figure. Added the general-industry disclosure to the summary, added 1926.102 (eye and face protection, replacing the checklist's 1910.133), and kept 1910.215 as the cited source.

Non-blocking: permanent mounting (1910.212(b)) and grounding/switch (1910.304/305) are cited in the checklist as general industry; construction electrical equivalents are Subpart K. Public domain, osha.gov. No UK wording.
